prize_parts.citation: For the development of general ligand-controlled palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling.

statement.case_for: I have moved from B051 to B057. In round 1 my objection was that C-N coupling might be a successful extension of the 2010 prize rather than a new concept. The exchange, and Somfai's answer in particular, changed that for me: the C-N problem had a different physical-organic bottleneck (amine binding and C-N reductive elimination from palladium amido complexes), it needed new ligand classes to overcome it, and it opened bond constructions that C-C coupling never reached. That is a distinct, mechanistically understood, ligand-controlled advance, not a repeat. It is also the only shortlisted achievement for which maturity, generality, independent confirmation, industrial use and clean attribution are all undisputed, and four members already treat it as their preferred configuration. Buchwald and Hartwig independently made the reaction general, which gives a two-name citation without strain.
statement.case_against: The overlap with the 2010 cross-coupling prize has not disappeared, and a methodology prize for a single bond type is narrower in conceptual reach than condensates or degraders. Kosugi and Migita's 1983 tin-amide coupling is a real precursor, and a two-name citation has to be worded around the general catalytic system, not the first observation, to be fair to that record. My own preferred B051 remains the more original idea in physical-chemical terms, and I am setting it aside because the in vivo phase status, the Pappu and Mittag credit problem and the field's age make it less ready, not because the concept lacks merit.

responses.point: Peter distinguishes C-N coupling from the 2010 prize on chemical grounds: a different bottleneck (amine binding and C-N reductive elimination) and new ligand classes, and he would keep two names and not add Kosugi.
responses.response: This is the argument I was missing and it answers the chair's question for me. The 2010 prize covered C-C bond formation with organometallic partners, whereas here the rate-limiting steps and the ligand design rules differ, so I no longer read it as an extension. I also agree with not adding a third name: the stoichiometric tin chemistry lacked amine scope and catalytic generality, and the citation should say 'general' and 'ligand-controlled' so the priority record is respected without diluting the pair.

responses.point: Heiner asks me to say which in vivo condensate claims are settled, and pairs B057 with base editing by Liu alone in a two-part configuration.
responses.response: On condensates, I can only claim what is settled: liquid-like behaviour and multivalent demixing in vitro, and good evidence in vivo for P granules and nucleoli. The functional role of most other assemblies, and whether they are equilibrium phases, is not settled, and that is why I no longer put B051 first. I do not support adding base editing as a second part. Its chemical step is the existing deamination reaction, the work is about a decade old with safety data still accruing, and a Liu-only credit leaves Komor, Gaudelli, Nishida and Kondo unresolved. A single-part B057 is a cleaner configuration than the pairing.

responses.point: Daniel argues that degraders introduce a new design principle that outweighs the maturity of C-N coupling, and he regards my B051 case as scientifically matured but not yet ready.
responses.response: I agree with your reading of B051 and have changed my position on it. On B004 I accept the induced-proximity design principle, but the PROTAC and cereblon glue strands are close to two discoveries that three names cannot honour, and no degrader is approved yet. Ciulli versus Handa for the third place is still open, so I keep B004 as an alternative to revisit once attribution is settled, not as my preferred part.

responses.point: Johan lists the 2010 overlap and the Kosugi priority question as the main objections to B057 and asks for the citation to reward the general catalytic system.
responses.response: I shared your first objection in round 1 and now consider it answered by the different bond type and ligand problem. I support your citation request: the wording 'general ligand-controlled' separates the prize from Kosugi's stoichiometric-in-tin coupling. You also call overdue recognition not an argument, and I agree; my support rests on demonstrated consequences and mechanistic clarity.

uncertainties: Whether the expert record confirms that Kosugi and Migita's tin-amide chemistry lacked the amine scope and catalytic generality that justify a two-name citation.
Whether a majority accepts C-N coupling as distinct enough from the 2010 prize, or still reads a second palladium prize as incremental.
Whether B051 will be ready in a later year once in vivo phase status and credit among Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen, Pappu and Mittag are clearer.
Whether B004 attribution between the PROTAC and glue strands can be resolved by the final ballot.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any shortlisted candidate. I am a Lund colleague of Heiner Linke and Peter Somfai, and I work on lipid self-assembly and amyloid, but I have no personal or institutional tie to Buchwald, Hartwig, or the other candidates. Somfai's field adjacency to B057 was disclosed in round 1 and does not alter my own assessment.
